label: Evaluation
summary: Runs a RAG system over benchmark questions, grades answers with an LLM judge and reports metrics.

children.label: RagSystem
children.summary: ABC: answer(question) returns a SystemAnswer; oracle and no-answer bound the scores.

children.label: evaluation/system.py
children.summary: RagSystem ABC, OracleSystem upper bound, NoAnswerSystem lower bound.
children.details: `RagSystem` is the ABC with the `name` ClassVar and abstract `answer`. `NOT_FOUND_ANSWER` is the shared refusal text used by all systems. `OracleSystem` is built from the questions and looks up the gold answer by question text; an unknown question gets the not-found answer. `NoAnswerSystem` ignores the question.

children.label: Blind systems
children.summary: A system sees only the question text, so the answer key cannot leak in.
children.details: `RagSystem.answer` takes a plain `str`, not a `Question`, so the gold answer, answer facts and expected doc ids are not reachable from inside a system. The class docstring states the reason: nothing from the answer key can leak in. Only `OracleSystem` is given the questions, deliberately, to act as the upper bound.

children.label: Registry
children.summary: Systems, judges and retrievers are looked up by name in registry.py, so the CLI can run any.
children.details: registry.py holds three dicts of factories: `SYSTEMS` (name -> factory taking the questions), `JUDGES` and `RETRIEVERS` (name -> factory taking the BM25 sample size). `evaluate()` does `SYSTEMS[system_name](questions)`, so adding a system is one dict entry. Factories are lambdas, so heavy objects (Gemini client, loaded pipeline, embedders) are only built for the chosen name.

children.label: evaluation/registry.py
children.summary: SYSTEMS, JUDGES and RETRIEVERS dicts of factories, plus the shared UsageMeter.
children.details: Builds the lookup tables the CLI uses. Also defines the module-level `USAGE` `UsageMeter` shared by the answer systems and the judge, which is how a run reports total Gemini cost. `RETRIEVERS` lists minilm-summary, minilm-chunk, gte-chunk, bm25, hybrid (no rerank) and hybrid-rerank; only bm25 uses the sample size, to find its on-disk index folder via `bm25_index_dir`.

The contract every evaluated system shares: `answer(question: str) -> SystemAnswer`, nothing else. `SystemAnswer` carries the answer text, `retrieved_doc_ids` (best first), optional `cited_doc_ids` and an optional agent `trace`.

A new variant subclasses `RagSystem`, sets the class-level `name` and implements `answer`; then it is added to `SYSTEMS` in registry.py to be runnable by name. The system receives only the question text, never the gold answer or expected documents.

Two reference systems bound the scale: `OracleSystem` (gold answer and expected docs, should score near 100%, so any gap is judge noise) and `NoAnswerSystem` (always the not-found answer, correct only on info-not-found questions).

children.label: hybrid-rerank
children.summary: Top 5 documents from the BM25 + gte + reranker pipeline go to Gemini, which cites its sources.

children.label: evaluation/pipeline_answer.py
children.summary: PipelineAnswerSystem: documents cut to 12k chars, CitedAnswer reports used docs.
children.details: `PipelineAnswerSystem.answer` retrieves, builds the prompt with `documents_context` (documents numbered from 1, each cut to `MAX_DOCUMENT_CHARS` = 12,000, about 3,000 tokens, which 95% of documents fit), and calls Gemini with a `CitedAnswer` response schema. `cited_doc_ids` maps cited numbers back to doc ids, dropping out-of-range numbers and repeats. An empty answer becomes `NOT_FOUND_ANSWER`. Tokens are counted into the `UsageMeter`.

children.label: evaluation/hybrid.py
children.summary: PipelineRetriever: sync Retriever over the async pipeline on a background event loop.
children.details: `PipelineRetriever` adapts the async `RetrievalPipeline` to the sync `Retriever` interface: it starts a private event loop in a daemon thread and submits `pipeline.run(...)` with `run_coroutine_threadsafe`, so database connections stay on one loop even when the evaluation's worker threads call it. It also offers `retrieve_keywords` (BM25 only, via `run_keywords`) for the agent and `searchable_doc_ids` for recall-vs-index reporting. `to_hits` converts documents to `SearchHit`, with `distance` as the negated rerank score (or fusion score without a reranker).

children.label: Rerank top 50, send top 5
children.summary: Reranking the fused top 50 gave the biggest recall gain, and five reranked documents beat ten unreranked.
children.details: The retrieval pipeline reranks the fused top 50 candidates and the answer system shows only the top 5 to Gemini. Article 002 found reranking gave the biggest recall gain and five reranked documents beat ten unreranked, so a short context is both better and cheaper. See `top_k=5` in `PipelineAnswerSystem` and the reranked `RETRIEVERS['hybrid-rerank']` entry.

The main answering system, registered as `hybrid-rerank`. Retrieval is `RetrievalPipeline.load()` (BM25 and gte-modernbert fused, then reranked) wrapped in `PipelineRetriever`. The top `top_k=5` documents are numbered in one prompt and Gemini returns structured JSON (`CitedAnswer`: answer plus the numbers of the documents used). Thinking is set LOW.

Unlike `summary-search` it reads whole documents (cut to 12,000 chars), and unlike `agent-rerank` it searches exactly once. `retrieved_doc_ids` is all five hits, `cited_doc_ids` is the subset the model used.

children.label: agent-rerank
children.summary: ReAct agent: starts from the pipeline's first search, then may search up to twice more.

children.label: evaluation/agent.py
children.summary: AgentSystem with Budget and overridable tools/can_call/run_tool hooks, MAX_SEARCHES=3.
children.details: `AgentSystem.answer` runs a manual tool loop (`automatic_function_calling` disabled): each model turn is appended to `contents` unchanged because it carries Gemini's thought signatures. The first search is automatic and counted in a `Budget` (searches, reads). Each tool call goes through the overridable `run_tool`, which returns the model's response and the documents found; a call past the limit gets an error (`LIMIT_REACHED`). `tools()` and `can_call(budget)` are hooks too, so `SnippetAgentSystem` subclasses it to change the tools and budget. `KnowledgeBase` is a Protocol with `retrieve` and `retrieve_keywords`, satisfied by `PipelineRetriever`. Tool declarations and trace steps now live in agent_tools.py. Prompts come from prompts.py. Searches are added to the `UsageMeter` at the end.

children.label: evaluation/agent_tools.py
children.summary: Gemini tool declarations for the agent searches and read, plus tool_step and model_step trace records.
children.details: Holds the tool names (`SEARCH_TOOL`, `KEYWORD_TOOL`, `READ_TOOL`) and `search_function`, which builds a one-query function declaration. `search_tools` gives the two searches of `agent-rerank`; `snippet_tools` gives the three of `agent-snippets` (general search, keyword search with snippet description, and `read_document` taking a `doc_id`). Descriptions come from prompts.py. `tool_step` and `model_step` build the `TraceStep` records, the latter including thoughts, tool calls and input, output and thinking tokens. Split out of agent.py so both agents share them.

children.label: Agent rescues search misses
children.summary: Most wrong answers were search failures, so the agent retries with its own wording; it rescued 6-9 of 50 misses.
children.details: Article 003 analysed why answers were wrong and found most were search failures rather than reading failures. The agent lets the model rewrite the query or switch to keyword search when the first result looks off. Per the article it rescued 6-9 of 50 misses.

Registered as `agent-rerank`. It first runs the same full-pipeline search on the question (counted as search 1), shows those top 5 documents to Gemini, then Gemini either answers or calls a tool: `search_knowledge_base` (the full pipeline with its own wording) or `keyword_search` (BM25 only, for exact names and ids). `MAX_SEARCHES = 3` counts the first one, so at most two more; once reached, function calling is switched to mode NONE and the next turn must answer.

Because it starts from the plain pipeline's result it can only add documents. `retrieved_doc_ids` is every document any search returned, in order found, and the full step-by-step `trace` is stored on the result.

The loop is built to be extended: `agent-snippets` (below) subclasses `AgentSystem` and overrides `tools`, `can_call` and `run_tool`.

children.label: summary-search
children.summary: Baseline: vector search over document summaries, Gemini answers from the closest ones.

children.label: evaluation/summary_search.py
children.summary: SummarySearchSystem: MiniLM summary retrieval, excerpts cut to 1,500 chars.
children.details: `SummarySearchSystem.answer` retrieves top 10 summaries, formats them with `context` (numbered, with source type, field and doc id) and asks Gemini for a free-text answer using the `summary_answer_instructions` prompt. `retrieved_doc_ids` are de-duplicated hit ids.

children.label: Weak by design
children.summary: Only documents with a summary are searchable; it scored 4.1% on basic questions, the baseline to beat.
children.details: The system can only find documents that have a summary, and only what the summary says. Article 002 reports it scoring 4.1% on basic questions; it is kept as the floor the pipeline systems must beat.

Registered as `summary-search`, the weak baseline. Retrieval is vector search (MiniLM embedder, the `summary` field) over per-document summaries, `top_k=10`; each excerpt is cut to `MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` = 1,500 and Gemini answers as plain text, with no citations and no usage metering. Differs from the other variants by never reading document bodies and by not using the retrieval pipeline.

children.label: agent-snippets
children.summary: Agent whose keyword search shows matching-line snippets and can read chosen documents in full.

children.label: evaluation/agent_snippets.py
children.summary: SnippetAgentSystem: 5 searches, 3 full reads, keyword results as snippets.
children.details: `SnippetAgentSystem` extends `AgentSystem` (name `agent-snippets`). `tools()` returns `snippet_tools()`; `can_call` is true while searches or reads remain; `run_tool` handles `read_document` and `keyword_search` itself and delegates the general search to the parent. Keyword search fetches `KEYWORD_RESULTS` = 10 hits, loads their full text with `read_documents` and shows `snippet_context` instead of the text. `read` returns one document cut at `READ_CHARS` = 30,000 with a cut marker, or an error when `MAX_READS` = 3 is used up or the id is unknown. `SnippetKnowledgeBase` is the Protocol adding `read_documents` to `KnowledgeBase`. `MAX_SEARCHES` is 5, counting the automatic first one.

children.label: evaluation/snippets.py
children.summary: Turns a document into the best matching passages for a keyword query.
children.details: `query_terms` tokenizes the query the way BM25 does (lowercase, stopwords removed, stemmed with the English Stemmer via `tokenize` from index_bm25). `matches` finds the words in a line that stem to a query term. `snippets` ranks lines by number of distinct query words then position, and shows up to `MAX_SNIPPETS` = 2, each with `CONTEXT_LINES` = 2 lines around it; a line over `LONG_LINE` = 500 chars becomes a 250-char window each side of the first match; lines already shown as context are skipped; with no match the first `FALLBACK_CHARS` = 300 characters are shown. `snippet_context` lays out one block per hit: number, source type, title, id, character count, then the snippets.

children.label: Snippets save tokens
children.summary: Full documents cost the most tokens, so keyword hits are previewed and only chosen ones read in full.
children.details: The module docstring in agent_snippets.py states the reason: showing each keyword result as matching lines plus context lets the agent scan twice as many results (10 against top_k=5) for fewer tokens, then read by id only the ones that look right, within a separate budget of 3 reads. The general search and the automatic first search still return full text.

Registered as `agent-snippets`. It is `agent-rerank` with a different keyword tool and one more tool. The first search and `search_knowledge_base` still return full document text (top 5). `keyword_search` returns 10 documents as short snippets: the lines matching the query with context, plus each document's id and length. The new `read_document` tool fetches one document in full by id, cut at 30,000 characters.

Budgets are separate: up to 5 searches in total (the automatic first counts) and 3 full reads; tools stay on while either has room. Needs a knowledge base with `read_documents`, which `PipelineRetriever` provides. Uses the `snippet_agent_instructions` prompt.

children.label: Files
children.summary: Entry points, grading, metrics, reporting and cost counting.

children.label: evaluate.py
children.summary: evaluate() and evaluate_search() entry points behind the two commands.
children.details: `evaluate()` wires the full run (questions from the DB, system and judge from the registry, `RunProgress` bar showing running Gemini cost, report printed at the end, returns the run id). `wrong_in` restricts to questions a previous run got wrong. `evaluate_search()` does the same for a retriever without an LLM.

children.label: evaluation/pipeline.py
children.summary: run_evaluation: threaded per-question answer, retrieval metrics and grade, stored in batches.
children.details: `evaluate_question` answers, computes `document_recall` and `invalid_extra_docs`, then grades; a system exception is stored as `system: ...` and a judge exception as `judge: ...` on the result. `evaluate_questions` maps this over a `ThreadPoolExecutor` (8 workers by default), keeping question order. `run_evaluation` creates the run, stores results in batches of `BATCH_SIZE` = 50, and finishes it with the `RunSummary`.

children.label: evaluation/judge.py
children.summary: AnswerJudge ABC and GeminiJudge grading correctness and fact coverage.
children.details: `AnswerJudge` is an ABC with `grade(question, answer) -> AnswerGrade`. `GeminiJudge` sends a prompt with question, reference answer, numbered facts and the answer (`grading_prompt`) and requires a JSON `AnswerGrade`. It raises `ValueError` if there is no verdict or if the number of fact flags differs from the question's `answer_facts`.

children.label: evaluation/metrics.py
children.summary: document_recall, invalid_extra_docs and run averages following the leaderboard.
children.details: `document_recall` is the share of expected ids found (None when none are expected). `invalid_extra_docs` counts distinct returned ids that were not expected. `summarize` averages over a set of questions and counts ungraded (failed) ones as 0 for score, so errors lower the result. `summarize_run` gives an overall summary plus one per question type.

children.label: evaluation/report.py
children.summary: format_report: per-question-type table with an overall row.
children.details: `format_report` prints a fixed-width table: one row per question type then an overall row, with columns questions, score, correct, complete, doc recall, extra docs and errors. `format_row` renders a single line; missing recall shows as a dash.

children.label: evaluation/retrieval.py
children.summary: Retrieval-only evaluation: recall@k per retriever, no LLM (evaluate-search).
children.details: `retrieval_metrics` averages recall@k over questions that expect documents, and `reachable`: the recall ceiling given which expected docs are in the index. `evaluate_retrieval` retrieves `max(ks)` documents per question (`DEFAULT_KS` = 1, 5, 10, 20) and returns metrics for `all` plus each question type. `format_retrieval_report` renders a markdown table.

children.label: evaluation/usage.py
children.summary: UsageMeter: thread-safe Gemini token counts and dollar cost.
children.details: `UsageMeter` adds up calls, input, output, thinking tokens and agent searches under a lock, since worker threads share it. `cost()` prices input at $0.75 and output (including thinking) at $3.75 per million tokens (Gemini 3.8 Flash standard). `report()` makes the one-line summary printed after each run.

The machinery around the systems: CLI entry points, the per-question run loop, the judge, metric maths, report formatting, a retrieval-only evaluation and token cost counting. None of these depends on which system is being evaluated.

children.label: Also uses
children.summary: Models, tables, storage and prompts the evaluation depends on.

children.label: models/evaluation.py
children.summary: SystemAnswer, QuestionResult, RunSummary and other result models.
children.details: Pydantic models for `SystemAnswer` (answer, retrieved and cited doc ids, trace), `TraceStep`, `AnswerGrade`, `QuestionResult`, `MetricSummary`, `RunSummary` and `RetrievalMetrics`.

children.label: tables/evaluation.py
children.summary: SQL tables for runs and question results.
children.details: SQL tables behind stored runs and per-question results.

children.label: repository/evaluation.py
children.summary: create_run, add_results, finish_run, wrong_question_ids.
children.details: `create_run` opens a run row, `add_results` stores a batch, `finish_run` saves the summary, `wrong_question_ids` gives the ids a run got wrong (used by `--wrong-in` reruns).

children.label: prompts.py
children.summary: Loads the answer, judge and agent prompt texts by name.
children.details: `prompt(name, **values)` loads a prompt text by name and fills in placeholders; used for answer, judge, agent and tool-description prompts.
Shared infrastructure the evaluation reads or writes: result models, the SQL tables and repository functions that store runs, and the prompt loader.

children.label: Score = correct x complete
children.summary: A wrong answer scores 0 however complete, matching the EnterpriseRAG-Bench leaderboard.
children.details: `metrics.py` states it follows the EnterpriseRAG-Bench leaderboard: the overall score is the mean of correctness times completeness per question, so an incorrect answer gets 0 however many facts it covers. Completeness comes from the judge's per-fact flags (`facts_covered`). Article 002 explains why results are reported this way.

children.label: Cost is reported
children.summary: Every run prints Gemini token cost, because answer cost drives the monthly RAG bill.
children.details: `UsageMeter` prints calls, tokens and dollars after every run, and `evaluate()` shows the running cost in the progress bar. Article 002-1 argues answer-time token cost dominates the RAG bill, which is why the 12,000-char document cut and top 5 are used.

children.label: Errors recorded
children.summary: A failing system or judge is stored on the question's result instead of stopping the run.
children.details: In `evaluate_question`, system and judge exceptions are caught and stored in `result.error` (`system: ...` or `judge: ...`). `summarize` counts such questions as 0, so failures lower the score instead of hiding, and the report has an errors column.

details:
Produces a scored report for one RAG system on the EnterpriseRAG-Bench questions, for whoever is comparing systems or tuning retrieval. `train-rag evaluate` runs a system plus a judge; `train-rag evaluate-search` measures retrieval recall alone with no LLM.

Flow of `evaluate()` in evaluate.py:
- load questions from the database (optionally one question type, a limit, or only those an earlier run got wrong)
- build the system and judge by name from registry.py
- `run_evaluation` answers and grades each question on a thread pool, stores the results in batches of 50, and returns a `RunSummary`
- print `format_report` and the Gemini cost line from `UsageMeter`

Questions and stored runs come from the repository/tables layer; the systems call the retrieval pipeline module (`RetrievalPipeline`) and Gemini. Read evaluation/system.py first, then pipeline.py.
